properties.description:
`release_without_manifest`: a Release with an AT_EPOCH edge, at least one DEPLOYED_TO edge and zero INCLUDES edges raises a gap at **severity 0.85, which FAILS `reflow2_check`** (default `--gap-threshold` 0.8). Anthony's call, 2026-08-21 — `dec:an-empty-manifest-on-a-shipped-release-stops-the-build`. It sits with the findings that say the design asserts something untrue, not with the questions that wait for a human, because a note was demonstrably not enough: the v0.38.0 cut passed the gate green with 96 notes scrolling past it.

Keys on structure and never on `status`, deliberately: rel:v0380 was tagged, published, deployed and asset-verified while its status still read `planned`, so a status-based exemption would have excused the single instance the rule exists for.

Guarded against flooding the same way `unreleased_component` is: if NO release in the design carries a manifest, release contents are simply not modelled here, and that is one whole-graph fact rather than one alarm per release. Measured against reflow2's own 40 releases before it was written — zero false positives — and then proved live by stripping v0.37.0's 275 INCLUDES edges from a copy of the real design and watching the gate go red.

A genuinely contentless release — a re-tag, a docs-only republish — stays acknowledgeable with a reason on the record. Red until somebody says why, never red forever.

The read half of the same capability: a cut ENDS by calling `release_report` for the new release and reading the counts. Hundreds of artifacts, components and capabilities is the healthy answer; `artifacts: []` means the manifest never landed. This is the eighth and last step of `flow:release-cut`.

Also hardened its sibling: `release_without_epoch` exempted any `planned` release, and now exempts one only while it is UNDEPLOYED — found by this detector's own tests. The sibling stays at 0.6 and stays a question, because which epoch a release belongs to is a judgement and its absence asserts nothing false.
properties.name: A release that is out and records shipping nothing stops the build, and a cut ends by reading it
